payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Add a helmet to the woman.
node.criteria: Apply the original rubric to the requested change only. Return yes when the evidence establishes that the woman has a helmet on her head and that adding it is a requested edit. Return no only when the evidence establishes that no requested change has progressed. Return partial when evidence establishes some progress toward adding the helmet but does not establish complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits do not count as progress. If the evidence does not establish which rubric outcome applies, return unknown. The endpoint inspection can establish completion on its own when it clearly shows the requested result; the comparison check is supporting evidence, not an additional completion requirement. If that check is skipped, do not treat it as not applicable or as a failure: use the endpoint evidence to decide whether completion is established, and otherwise return unknown unless other evidence establishes progress or no progress. Supporting observations do not earn completion credit independently.
node.binding: Target: The woman is wearing or otherwise visibly has a helmet on her head.. Reference: The woman in the input image..

node_traces.evidence: The edited image clearly shows the woman wearing a helmet, and the comparison confirms it was added as requested.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image clearly shows the woman wearing a helmet on her head.
Comparison shows a helmet was added to the woman’s head in the edited image.

response.content: {"text":"The node is already well calibrated for this case: the edited image visibly shows a helmet on the woman’s head, and the trace reports complete fulfillment with strong endpoint and comparison evidence. No semantic change is indicated by this successful evaluation. For robustness in future cases, preserve the distinction between endpoint evidence of completion and comparison evidence that supports whether the requested edit was added; do not make both checks mandatory or count supporting observations as independent progress. Keep the target bound to the woman in the source image and the criterion focused on a helmet visibly worn on her head. The abbreviated binding in the evaluated input is less precise than the full node binding, so ensure typed edits retain that target and criterion clarity. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported."}
